title: Artifact-reference pinning policy and SDK priority matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need an unambiguous, discoverable, and backward-compatible way to pin model versions from the API/SDK. Current semantics (tag / semver / branch) are underspecified and lead to differences between SDKs and the runtime fallback behavior, which complicates rollouts and performance guarantees.

Goal: Define a single canonical artifact-reference format and a deterministic precedence matrix for pin resolution. Publish mapping rules for SDKs and ensure performance profile attachments (published by model owners) are considered during resolution. Provide clear fallback rules so runtime behavior is predictable and testable.

Scope: API surface (model identifier grammar), SDK mapping helpers, runtime resolver spec (precedence + fallbacks), and test matrix + e2e tests. Not in scope: UI for pin management (will be separate PM ticket).

Key constraints: must preserve backwards compatibility with existing simple tags (e.g., "stable") and semver expressions; must enable commit-level reproducibility (via immutable commit hashes); must allow performance profile binding so callers can request only variants with published profiles for their workload class.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts artifact refs in the canonical form 'owner/model@ref' where ref can be: tag:<name> | semver:<expr> | commit:<hex>'
SDK helpers expose 'resolveModelRef()' that returns an ordered list of candidate artifact refs with their attached performance_profile_id when available
Resolution precedence is fully documented and enforced by runtime tests and SDK unit tests
If a performance_profile_id is requested, resolver filters out candidates without published profiles for the requested profile class
Runtime fallback behavior: when a higher-precedence ref is unavailable, automatically attempt next candidate and emit structured telemetry and an event to the user's rollout dashboard
Compatibility tests demonstrating older simple refs still resolve to the same model as today unless pinned explicitly by commit

decisions: Canonical artifact ref format chosen: owner/model@ref
Ref types supported: tag:<name>, semver:<expr>, commit:<hex> (sha256 recommended), latest (legacy)
Precedence: explicit commit > exact tag > pinned tag (org-level pin) > semver exact match > semver range match > legacy latest
SDKs will implement a 'resolveModelRef' that returns ordered candidates with attached performance_profile_id when present
When a performance_profile_class is requested (e.g., 'latency-1k', 'cost-optimized'), resolver must filter to candidates that have published profiles for that class unless caller opts out
Telemetry: any deviation from top-precedence resolution must emit structured event with reason and candidate list
implementation_plan: 1) Publish RFC and get review approvals (this ticket)
2) Add grammar and validation to API contract and server-side resolver (runtime)
3) SDKs: add 'resolveModelRef' helper and a convenience 'pinTo(commit|tag|semver)' functions
4) Model registry: ensure performance_profile metadata is queryable in the registry API (model owners publish profiles via console or registry API)
5) Tests: unit tests for semver parsing, integration tests with staging model registry, e2e tests that exercise fallback telemetry
6) Docs: update public API docs and migration guide for existing customers
api_examples: SDK resolve example (TypeScript): const candidates = await client.resolveModelRef('acme/opt-13b@semver:>=2.1.0 <3.0.0', { profileClass: 'latency-1k' }) // returns ordered refs with performance_profile_id
review_feedback: Luis Ortega (PM): Ensure we capture multi-tenant org-level pins in precedence; added test case where org pin should override repo tag for enterprise customers.
Zoe Kim (Design): UX should show resolved immutable commit to users when a ref resolves to a different commit than requested; accept but hide in compact views.
Ravi Shah (Eng): Prefer using semver npm library for parsing rather than hand-rolled regex to avoid prerelease corner cases.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Semver range resolution may match unexpected releases (pre-releases). Mitigation: explicit semver parsing lib + configurable includePrereleases flag
Risk: Customers rely on 'latest' behavior. Mitigation: Deprecate 'latest' with long notice, provide migration guide and compatibility mode opt-in
Risk: Performance profile coverage incomplete for older models. Mitigation: Resolver returns candidates even without profiles but annotates them and only filters when caller requests profileClass
